headline: 409 deaths: Dengue death toll crosses 400 in Bangladesh
summary: Nine more people died in the last 24 hours, with nearly 2,000 new hospital admissions reported across the country.
details: Nine more people have died from dengue in Bangladesh over the past 24 hours, according to official figures. This brings the total death toll for the year to 409.
A total of 1,982 patients were admitted to hospitals across the country within the last day. Dhaka Division recorded the highest number of admissions with 816 cases.
Other regional admissions include Chattogram with 313, Rajshahi with 217, Khulna with 214, Barishal with 194, Rangpur with 116, Mymensingh with 97, and Sylhet with 28.
So far this year, 130,219 dengue patients have been hospitalised nationwide, according to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS).
The DGHS has been recording hospitalisations and deaths since 2000. The worst year on record was 2023, when 1,705 people died and 321,179 patients were admitted.
caption:
409 deaths and over 130,000 hospitalisations so far this year. Dengue continues to claim lives across Bangladesh.

Nine more people have died from dengue in Bangladesh over the past 24 hours, according to official figures. This brings the total death toll for the year to 409.

A total of 1,982 patients were admitted to hospitals across the country within the last day. Dhaka Division recorded the highest number of admissions with 816 cases.

Other regional admissions include Chattogram with 313, Rajshahi with 217, Khulna with 214, Barishal with 194, Rangpur with 116, Mymensingh with 97, and Sylhet with 28.

So far this year, 130,219 dengue patients have been hospitalised nationwide, according to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS).

The DGHS has been recording hospitalisations and deaths since 2000. The worst year on record was 2023, when 1,705 people died and 321,179 patients were admitted.

headline_marked: Govt doesn't want [[enforced disappearances, extrajudicial killings]], says Home Minister
headline: Govt doesn't want enforced disappearances, extrajudicial killings, says Home Minister
summary: Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed promises to end the culture of disappearances and rehabilitate victims' families after meeting them in Parliament.
details: Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed stated that the government does not want enforced disappearances, extrajudicial killings, or deaths in police custody.
caption:
No more disappearances: the Home Minister promises a permanent end to the culture of enforced disappearances in Bangladesh.

Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed stated that the government does not want enforced disappearances, extrajudicial killings, or deaths in police custody.
